business_problem: Ceto needed a more scalable and reliable way to process high-frequency vessel sensor data for predictive maritime analytics after its previous platform could not keep up with fleet growth.
solution_summary: Ceto rebuilt its maritime analytics platform around MongoDB Atlas and Time Series Collections so it could ingest high-frequency vessel telemetry and turn it into predictive maintenance insights at scale. Each vessel emits thousands of sensor signals at 50-100Hz, creating around 300-400MB of raw data per day and about 90,000 JSON documents containing 100 time-series measurements. Ceto configured Atlas clusters to handle that throughput, then used Time Series Collections to compress, store, and query readings efficiently while preserving a single operational platform. Real-time processing on top of those collections lets the company analyze fleet conditions as data arrives, helping it predict failures, lower fuel consumption, and reduce operational risk. The architecture also gives Ceto headroom to expand from a handful of vessels to a much larger connected fleet without rewriting its data model or accepting downtime.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the scalable cluster layer that Ceto uses to ingest and process fleet telemetry continuously.

solution_components.name: Time Series Collections
solution_components.role: Stores and compresses high-frequency vessel sensor readings for real-time predictive analytics.

data_flow: Thousands of vessel sensors stream telemetry into MongoDB Atlas, where Time Series Collections compress and store the readings; real-time analytics then process those series to flag likely failures, support maintenance decisions, and feed operational insights back to maritime teams.
business_outcome: Ceto reduced storage needs from 300MB to 3MB per vessel per day, saved about $20,500 per vessel annually through predictive maintenance, and created a platform that can scale to much larger fleets.
